feature: Words sit in the middle of the box they are centred in
summary: A label centred inside a control now lands on the middle of it. A text box is kept a few points taller than its words so glyph edges have room to round into, and two places were sharing that room out as if it were part of the words: the starter controls put their labels two points high, and text told to sit in the middle or at the bottom of a box it has room in sat about two points low or hung through the floor.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to turn on: this is how every label is placed.

try.do: Open the Library and switch it to Comps.
Drag the Badge tile onto the canvas and look at the 3 in it.
Drag the Button tile onto the canvas and look at the word in it.
Drag the Nav Bar tile onto the canvas and look at Title against the bar behind it.
Double click the Button's word, type something much longer, and press Return.
Drag the Button's right edge much wider and check the word is still on the middle.
Press the text tool, click on the canvas, type a word, then press Middle in the Text section's Down row.

evaluate: Does the 3 in the Badge look like it is sitting on the middle of the pill, or still a hair high or low?
Does the Button's word look level with the middle of the button when you cover the rest of the screen?
Does the Nav Bar title look centred against the bar drawn behind it?
Is a half point of slop in either direction fine, or do you want these on the exact middle even when that means a half point frame?
The last step does nothing at all. Is a Down row that cannot move anything on a plain text box worth having on screen there?
rough: The task said a Nav Bar title sits two points low. It does not: measured off a real render it is centred to within half a point, and always was. The error was the other way and in two other places, so the fix is real but the report it came from was wrong about where.

The Down row (Top, Middle, Bottom) does nothing on a plain text box, because a text box on the canvas is always exactly as tall as its words: dragging its bottom edge moves it, dragging a corner re-wraps it, and neither leaves it any room. Down only bites when a container stretches the box. The second screenshot is that non-event, and it is filed as its own task.

So the half of this fix that lives in the renderer, words going down the box a person sees rather than the stored one, is proven by reading the ink off real rasters at eight samples per point rather than by a click path in the app. The starters half is the one in the picture.

Half a point of slop stays: a control whose height and words differ by an odd number cannot put its label on the exact middle and keep every frame on a whole point. The Button and the Badge each sit half a point low for that reason.
